title: Region-pin onboarding: simulated customer journeys and operator notes
content:
Purpose

This is a working simulation doc: run multiple synthetic customer onboarding journeys to surface gaps in our region-pin UX, operator handoffs, telemetry, and SLA/cost expectations. Goal is to produce concrete checklist items and edge-case scripts for the operator runbook and for Sales/CS to set expectations.

Short summary of outcomes (TL;DR)
- Basic flows (customer requests EU pin, we provision EU anchor + local cache) worked in 98/100 simulated signups.
- Two categories of failure observed: (1) routing drift when tenant IP geolocation differed from billing address (approx 1.7% of flows), and (2) transient fallback to global pool during autoscale spikes (0.9% of flows).
- Key friction spots: consent UI language ambiguity, unclear contract clause mapping for multi-region tenants, lack of operator-visible evidence package for some exception flows.

Test setup
- Synthetic tenant profiles (N=120): small single-tenant SaaS, mid-market analytics, enterprise financial, medical-imaging OEM.
- Traffic model: ramp from 10 rps to 700 rps over 15m to simulate onboarding load+warmup.
- Topology variants: EU-only, US-only, hybrid (EU pin with US backup), sovereign-on-prem anchor.
- Failure injection: simulated 15% packet loss to EU anchor for 2m in 30% of runs to exercise fallback.
- Metrics collected: routing decision logs, tenant-pin metadata, token serving region per request, KV cache hit/miss ratio, end-to-end P50/P95 latency, billing-account country vs request IP mapping.

Observed sequences and impact notes
1) IP vs billing mismatch (1.7%):
- Customer registers billing address: Germany, but initial onboarding calls come from a US-based CI/CD worker (ip=34.x.x.x). Routing policy picks US-edge (region unpinned because we treat first active region as anchor in the current onboarding flow).
- Impact: customer sees resources created in wrong region (violates residency expectation).
- Operator mitigation observed: manual re-pin required. Evidence package generation currently requires multiple logs stitched across tracing and tenant metadata; takes ~12–18 minutes.
- Suggested product fix: require explicit region selection in onboarding for contracts that include residency clause OR use billing-country as the authoritative initial pin when billing country != request country.

2) Autoscale spike fallback (0.9%):
- Scenario: pinned EU pool hits capacity, smart routing temporarily falls back to global pool in another region per our fallback policy.
- Impact: token-serving region mismatches pin; temporary SLA breaches and potential compliance exposure.
- Telemetry gap: fallback event is logged but not surfaced as an ‘‘audit-level residency violation’’ in the customer-facing evidence pack.
- Suggested ops change: create automatic alert and evidence bundle when fallback target != pinned region and mark incident as residency-exception-type.

3) Sovereign anchor onboarding friction:
- For on-prem anchors we observed configuration drift between the customer-manageable PKI and our anchor registration endpoint causes failed heartbeats in 8% of these synthetic runs.
- Root causes found: clock skew, cert chain mismatch, and network egress rules.
- Operator checklist items created (below).

Operator-visible artifacts to add (draft checklist)
- At signup: capture explicit region pin choice checkbox + billing-country fallback toggle. Add quick-link to contract clause (region pin).
- Post-provision verification (automated script): verify anchor health, assert KV cache routing table includes tenant pin, and produce an evidence bundle (signed manifest + request-sample traces) that is customer-downloadable.
- On fallback: auto-generate residency-violation incident (severity=high), notify CS and customer via templated email + include evidence pack.
- For on-prem anchors: heartbeat sanity-check tool (run as part of initial registration), cert-chain validator, time-sync check (NTP), and a networking egress test that simulates router-level DNS failures.

Customer-facing messaging & Sales enablement notes
- Sales play: include a short script to surface that the platform may temporarily fall back in capacity emergencies but will generate an audit package; give customers the option to disable fallbacks for strict residency contracts.
- Contract template suggestion: add a clause with three levels: 1) Preferred pin (best-effort), 2) Contractual pin with audit evidence required for any fallback, 3) Strict pin (no fallback allowed, may incur capacity/resourcing surcharge).
- Example email snippet for incident: "We experienced a temporary routing fallback for your tenant. We've prepared an evidence packet confirming request routing and timestamps — please find the attached manifest and remediation plan. Contact your CSM to discuss a permanent fix."

Telemetry/observability changes (minimal viable set)
- New telemetry events: residency_violation_detected, fallback_target_region, pin_decision_source (billing|signup_ip|admin_api).
- Dashboard: per-tenant residency incidents, weekly rollup for customers with >1 violation, heatmap of billing-country vs request-country mismatches.
- Sampling: store full traces for first 10 residency incidents per tenant for 90 days; after that store aggregated stats.

Simulated numbers and cost sensitivity (rough)
- Scenario A (mid-market app, EU pin): baseline cost per 10k tokens = $X (internal cost model), fallback to global increased infra egress and inter-region transfer cost by ~12–18% in our sim.
- Scenario B (enterprise strict pin, no fallback): required capacity reserve increases committed cost by ~27% vs dynamic shared pool but reduces violation risk to near-zero.
- Note: we used synthetic token size distribution with mean=45 tokens and 95th=210 tokens; real customers will vary widely — we need a lightweight cost-estimator in onboarding.

Unresolved questions / decision points
- Which source should win when billing-country != first-active-ip? (billing-country currently recommended) — need legal signoff for EU/UK/DE customers.
- Default fallback policy for enterprise tier: should we disable fallback by default for enterprise/strict plans? (Impacts bin-packing and economics.)
- Evidence bundle format: signed JSON manifest + log archive vs PDF summary + signed manifest — which do customers prefer for audit/contract purposes?

Next action items (owners + rough ETA)
- Implement onboarding UI change: explicit region selection + billing fallback toggle — owner: Lina Chen — ETA: 2024-11-30 (MVP).
- Telemetry events + incident classification change — owner: Mateo Ruiz — ETA: 2024-12-07.
- Operator runbook additions (scripts & evidence pack generation) — owner: Ravi Iyer — ETA: 2024-12-05.
- Draft contract language options for Legal & Sales review — owner: Asha Patel (author) — ETA: 2024-11-25.

Notes to self / things to test next round
- Run with a cohort of real customer metadata (anonymized) to validate billing-country heuristic accuracy.
- Add a simulation where tenant moves between regions (migration scenario) and measure operator time-to-fix and data movement cost.
- Validate on-prem anchor registration across major customer firewall setups (Fortinet, Palo Alto, Cisco ASA).

Appendix: quick operator run scripts (sketch)
- verify-anchor.sh <tenant> -> checks heartbeat, cert chain, ntp drift, returns PASS/FAIL and a short reason
- collect-evidence.sh <tenant> <time-window> -> bundles traces, routing-decision-logs, signed manifest (include pin_decision_source), zips and uploads to evidence storage with access token for customer
- re-pin-api example: POST /v1/tenants/<id>/pin {"region":"eu-west-1","reason":"manual re-pin after billing mismatch"} -- returns job id and estimated TTL for KV cache rebind.

End of draft — comments welcome.

(Will convert to a nicer runbook page after we validate on 50 real signups.)
